newsitem.title: FRANCE: Convicted French politician tries hand at acting.
newsitem.headline: Convicted French politician tries hand at acting.

text.p: Convicted ex-Lyon mayor Michel Noir said on Thursday he was trying his hand as an actor, taking a part in a production of Chekhov's "Uncle Vanya".

Noir, sentenced twice this year for corruption while running France's second-largest city, would be the second convicted politician to seek a comeback in acting. The production will open next week in the southern city of Aurillac.

Former businessman, cabinet minister and soccer boss Bernard Tapie, who faces jail sentences for tax fraud and rigging a soccer match, has a starring role in "Men, Women: Instructions for Use", the recently released film by French director Claude Lelouche.

Tapie, a flamboyant leftist, recently was forced to give up his seat in the French National Assembly after a court finding that he was bankrupt, a ruling that bars him from public office for five years.
The conservative Noir was found guilty of using Lyon's municipal funds to finance political campaigns and personal expenses.
Once tipped as a possible presidential candidate, he was trade minister when President Jacques Chirac was prime minister in 1986-88.
